Russell Transfer, a regulated motor carrier, submitted economic and demographic data on the Roanoke Valley region of Virginia which demonstrates that the migration of business and industry to suburban areas is not a phenomenon confined to the major cities. In recent years the areas surrounding Roanoke and Salem, Va., have undergone increased residential, commercial, and industrial development. Many industries formerly located in the cities have relocated in suburban industrial parks due to their need for additional space and new facilities, or as a result of urban renewal. This carrier, while generally supporting the proposed expansion, urges that Roanoke be accorded an even larger commercial zone (15 miles) than it would have under the proposed population-mileage formula.
<u>expansion</u>. - These carriers argue generally that there has been no significant migration of business to the suburbs since the present commercial zone regulations were adopted, or that such migration which has occurred has been to suburbs within the presently defined zone. Some carrier interests argue that movement to the suburbs is insignificant compared to migration from one geographic region to another or from the cities to points far outside the present zones.
